title: AttnRes weight loading ignores first_layer_idx: a pipeline rank silently loads another rank's queries
body:
Found during Kimi-K3 2-rank bring-up (#53508). Index: #54814. Fixed on `feature/kimi-k3-prefill`.

## What

`load_attn_res_weights` took the rank-LOCAL layer count and no offset, while the tensorbin cache and the checkpoint are both keyed by GLOBAL layer index. A rank holding layers 36..71 asked for `layers.0..35`.

Every name it asked for exists — the cache holds all 93 layers — so `check_cache_complete` returned True and the rank came up **scoring every AttnRes read with another rank's query**. No error, no warning, a plausible model.

## Why it survived

Nothing catches it:

- the cache is complete for the names requested, so the completeness check passes
- the shapes are identical (one folded query per layer), so nothing downstream objects
- single-rank runs have `first_layer_idx = 0`, where local and global indices coincide — so the entire existing suite is blind to it by construction

## Fix

Thread `first_layer_idx` through the naming and the checkpoint fold:

- [`_cache_artifact_names`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/752fce2c47b63470a83724c689011d17af5b86ee/models/demos/deepseek_v3_d_p/tt/attn_res/weights.py#L35) — `layers.{first_layer_idx + idx}`
- [`check_cache_complete`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/752fce2c47b63470a83724c689011d17af5b86ee/models/demos/deepseek_v3_d_p/tt/attn_res/weights.py#L100) — same window, or it verifies someone else's files are present
- [`load_attn_res_weights`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/752fce2c47b63470a83724c689011d17af5b86ee/models/demos/deepseek_v3_d_p/tt/attn_res/weights.py#L174) — offset in `place(...)`
- `fold_queries` / `query_weight_names` / `validate_query_weights` in `reference/kimi_k3/attn_res/weights.py` — same, for the state-dict path

Pinned by hardware-free tests in `tests/attn_res/model/test_attn_res_pipeline_split.py`, including that two ranks request **disjoint** windows (sharing only the model-level `output` query).

## Related

Same local-vs-global confusion as #54843. A third instance: `schedule.mla_layer_ids` is the whole MODEL's list, so the common `mla_layer_ids[:num_mla_layers]` idiom yields 3/7/11 for every rank and is correct only at `first_layer_idx = 0` — it scored a rank-1 layer-15 KV slab against layer 3's golden and reported PCC 0.006. Worth auditing every `first_layer_idx`-adjacent accessor for the same shape of bug.
